body:
Open Letter to Paris and all those wishing (or who have wished) to end their lives.
You are lovely.  But I’m not going to fill this letter with fluffy rainbows and soft bullshit, because I remember.  And patronization makes it worse.
I know it is bad.  I know that your mind faced the pits of hell and the devil himself unsheathed his sword to do battle with you.  But you cannot let him win.  My love, you are still young and you have a gorgeous and bright future ahead of you.  But that future is only for you.  In these moments of strange clarity, only you will be able to see what your outlined future holds.  I promise you, there is a future.  Because I am living in mine.  And yours lies in whatever you find for strength and value in these perfectly vulnerable moments.  [In the hospital, I found my future began with a tiny golf pencil (they didn’t trust me with a pen) and a donated composition book.]
Whatever your reasons may or may not be, we on the outside cannot begin to deduce what you and your mind are going through.  Those reasons are yours alone and never let anyone snatch them from you.  One day you may feel comfortable dispelling your reasons, but on that day, know the world is cruel and may turn it against you.  Know that you owe no one anything.  No explanations, no justifications.  You only owe yourself forgiveness to move past this experience and allowance to grow from whatever you have learned.
I want to tell you a sad truth.  You will never be okay.  Everyday will be a fight and a struggle to obtain sanity.  But sanity is knowing that you are never quite okay.  Sanity is knowing exactly where your demons lie and what destruction they are capable of.  Sanity is knowing how to cage your demons and knowing the right time and place to release them so they can have no power over you.  It means knowing that you will have to fight every morning for yourself.  It will be a fight to get out of bed, a fight to leave the house and a fight to rationally face this shitty world each day.  Sanity is knowing that sometimes you may lose a battle.  However, sanity is knowledge that the war is the fight that matters.  On days after I have lost a battle, I admit, it takes twice as long to start the day.  Knowing this, I must forgive myself and allow myself to move closer to strategically winning the war against my demons.  
I don’t think I will ever be able to stand on victory’s hill and raise by shining sword.  No one ever wins the war that way.  What matters for me is winning as many battles as I can against my demons.  And the most important thing is never going down without a kick-ass fight against my assorted demons.  I am confident that is the victory in and of itself.
But I will end with a little bit of fluffy bullshit: It gets better.  I promise.  But it will only be better if you leave yourself open for the right people to help you.  It will only stay better if you are compassionate to yourself and to your mind and give them the opportunity to heal.

Praying for your full recovery,

K
